title: The geometric stalks of a constructible sheaf of modules are finite
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $\mathcal F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite set; in particular, with the $\Lambda$-module structure induced by the $\Lambda$-module structures of the groups $\mathcal F(U)$, it is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules, line 12412 ff.): 'every stalk F_x is a finite type Lambda-module'; from Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) and Definition 03RW (definition-constructible) with Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback: stalk of an inverse image)

proof.text: *The stratum through $t$.* Let $t\in T$ be the point under $\bar t$. Choose a stratification $(\iota_k:Z_k\to T)_{k<n}$ with strata $T_k=\iota_k(Z_k)$ as in the definition of constructibility [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], [def-constructible-stratification]. The $T_k$ cover $T$, so $t\in T_k$ for some $k$; fix such $k$ and $z\in Z_k$ with $\iota_k(z)=t$.

source.place: Definition 03RW (definition-constructible): a finite partition of T into locally closed (constructible) strata

proof.text: *$\bar t$ factors through the stratum.* Since $\iota_k$ is an immersion and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ maps the unique point to $t=\iota_k(z)\in\iota_k(Z_k)$, [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-immersion] (2) gives a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z_k$ (same algebraically closed field $\Omega$) with $\iota_k\circ\bar z=\bar t$.

source.place: Schemes, discussion before Lemma 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points) with Definition 01IO (definition-immersion)

proof.text: *Stalk of the inverse image.* Let $G=\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal F$, the inverse image of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; its underlying abelian sheaf is the inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ (the inverse image of module sheaves is the same functor, by the convention of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]). By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] applied to $f=\iota_k:Z_k\to T$, the geometric point $\bar y=\bar z$ of $Z_k$ and the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$, whose image point is $\iota_k\circ\bar z=\bar t$ (Step 2), there is an isomorphism of abelian groups, in particular a bijection of sets, $G_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_{\bar t}$, stalks taken as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

*The stalk on the stratum is finite.* By clause (b) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], $G=\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_{Z_k}$-modules on $(Z_k)_{\Et}$ with an etale covering $\{U_i\to Z_k\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ such that $G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$; this is condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values] for $Y=Z_k$, $\mathcal G=G$. By (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of that lemma, $G$ is finite [def-constructible-finite]: the underlying set of its stalk at every geometric point is finite; $\bar z$ is such a point, an algebraically closed field being separably closed. The stalk there is the stalk of $G$ as a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules, the colimit in $\Lambda$-modules of $G(V)$ over the pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar z$; this index category is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (1), (2), applied with $R=\Lambda$ and with $R=\mathbf Z$, the colimit in $\Lambda$-modules and the colimit in abelian groups (the stalk $G_{\bar z}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf, [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]) are both the set of germs $(V,\bar v,a)$, $a\in G(V)$, modulo the same relation (equal after pulling back to a common refinement), so they have the same underlying set. Hence $G_{\bar z}$ is a finite set.

source.place: Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) and Definition 03RW (definition-constructible); the stalk as a colimit over etale neighbourhoods, Section 03PN (section-stalks)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By Steps 3 and 4, $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ is in bijection with the finite set $G_{\bar z}$, so it is finite. With its $\Lambda$-module structure (the colimit of the $\Lambda$-modules $\mathcal F(U)$, whose underlying abelian group is $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ by the comparison of Step 4 applied to $\mathcal F$ and $\bar t$) it is generated by its finitely many elements, hence a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against 095N/03RU/03RW: correct). Proof in five steps: the geometric point lies over a point of some stratum T_k = iota_k(Z_k); it factors through the immersion iota_k (new node lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-immersion: residue fields are preserved by immersions, so Spec(Omega) -> T lifts, Stacks 01IO/01HK/01J9/01L7); the stalk of iota_k^{-1}F at the lift is the stalk of F at t-bar (lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ, 03Q1); iota_k^{-1}F is finite locally constant with finite values, so its geometric stalks are finite (lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values (1)=>(2)), the module stalk and the abelian stalk having the same underlying set (filtered colimits of modules are computed on elements: lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered, lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise); a finite module is finitely generated.
